The SRR unit cell is a cubic structure with 2.5 mm sides.
The SRR outer ring size is 2.2 mm with a width of 0.2 mm and an opening width of 0.3 mm.
The substrate permittivity for the SRR is 4.4 with thickness 0.25 mm.
The SRR resonates near 9.75 GHz with negative permeability and refractive index.
The microstrip antenna substrate is RF4 with permittivity 4.4 and thickness 2.8 mm.
The antenna patch size is 6.6 mm by 6.6 mm.
The ground plane size is 40 mm by 40 mm.
The antenna operates at 10.2 GHz and is fed by a coaxial line.
The PBG structure consists of square holes of 4.8 mm by 4.8 mm with a period of 7.2 mm around the antenna.
The PBG structure increases antenna gain from 5.37 dB to 6.07 dB (an improvement of 0.7 dB).
The SRR cover does not change the antenna gain but reduces RCS significantly.
The antenna bandwidth after adding PBG and SRR cover is 1.4 GHz.
The SRR units are arranged vertically with a 4 mm period and placed 2.5 mm above the patch.
The RCS reduction is up to 21.05 dB, with tangential direction RCS reduced from -31.32 dB to -52.37 dB.
Normal direction RCS is reduced from -16.24 dB to -24.23 dB by the SRR cover.
The SRR cover causes scattering waves to deviate from the mirror direction, reducing RCS.
The PBG structure inhibits surface waves, improving radiation efficiency and directivity.
The SRR exhibits left-handed material properties (negative permeability and refractive index) near resonance.
The antenna design balances stealth (low RCS) and performance (high gain and bandwidth).
The study uses simulation to validate antenna gain, return loss, radiation patterns, and RCS.
